content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm new to using [product_name] [article_no] and would appreciate your guidance with a few issues. I'm working on a project to detect and remove damaged items from a production line, using two TOR sensors assigned to the ejection and detection zones, each with its own counter. Since the ejection zone is distant from the detection zone, I need to record the index (counter value) of detected damaged items. Considering the production pace, I need to store at least four values. I previously tried adding a third counter that resets after every four damaged items, but it didn't solve the problem. Any suggestions or ideas would be welcomed. Thank you!
I've made two sample approaches for saving analog values: one is not protected against voltage failure, and the other includes voltage failure safety.
Thank you [user_name] for your reply; your input was very helpful!

analysis.insight_summary: A user encountered challenges storing multiple analog or counter values in a [product_name] controller ([article_no]) for a production line inspection task. Attempts to resolve this with a counter mechanism proved insufficient for reliably keeping at least four values. Another user responded by sharing two example solutions, one incorporating voltage failure safety, which helped resolve the issue.
